summary: A small computer model, rather than tests on people, gave fostamatinib a high score for potential liver problems and a low score for potential heart problems [M]. Official warnings state that patients should have their blood pressure checked every two weeks until stable, and then monthly, to watch for high blood pressure [3]. These warnings also advise monthly monitoring of liver function tests to check for liver damage, with doses being paused or reduced if test levels rise [3]. Additionally, one clinical study was recommended to stop enrolling patients and providing the medication, while other trials ended when a company decided to discontinue developing the drug for a joint condition called rheumatoid arthritis [5][6][7].
